As a component of this course, learners will take up to two ATI RN Comprehensive Predictor Proctored Assessments,
which is a nationally normed, standardized exam. The score a learner earns provides information regarding the
probability of success for passing this content area on the NCLEX®. This information is based on statistical analysis of
nursing student exam results from across the country.
Prior to taking the ATI RN Comprehensive Predictor Proctored Assessment:
Each learner is required to take RN ATI Comprehensive Practice Assessment (ATI) Practice Assessment A and B and
perform remediation on the first attempt of each practice assessment as assigned below. Failure to complete the ATI
and remediation process will result in forfeiture of the next (I or II) attempt.
After taking the ATI Proctored Assessment:
The learner will receive the following information in his/her ATI account:
a. an individualized score report indicating performance on specific subject areas; and
b. an individualized remediation plan developed by ATI to help prepare the learner for success on the NCLEX-RN®.

slides.title: The rationale for remediation is that students are ultimately responsible for their own learning and will need to
text: The rationale for remediation is that students are ultimately responsible for their own learning and will need to
demonstrate competency to progress in the nursing course. This remediation process helps ensure that learners
understand the content and improve the potential for success in their subsequent courses and on the NCLEX. The first
attempt on each assessment provides the most accurate demonstration of the student’s current knowledge of the
Faculty are responsible for managing the administration of the ATI practice and proctored exams, including the
Comprehensive examinations will be administered to students during the final quarter in their program. Three fifty-item
examinations are given as a final assessment of students’ knowledge gained throughout the program. The blueprint of
these examinations reflects the test blueprint of the NCLEX-RN®. Students will have the opportunity to review the topics
of questions which were answered incorrectly upon completion of the exam.
Accurate computation of medication dosages and solutions is an essential competency for safe nursing practice. To
establish the achievement of this competency, students will be required to obtain a passing score of 90% or higher on a
medication calculation test. Students will have three attempts to achieve the passing score or higher. Remediation will
be required after each unsuccessful attempt on the medication calculation test. Failure to complete the remediation
process will result in forfeiture of the next attempt. If a student does not earn a passing grade of 90% or higher by the
third attempt, the student will earn a grade of “F” for this course.

slides.title: Clinical and CLL Written Assignments:
text: Students may be required to submit written assignments. Successful completion of these assignments will be based on
earning a pass as outlined in the grading rubrics included in the syllabus. Students who do not pass a written assignment
(i.e.: Careplan, Concept Maps and Teaching Plans) will have one opportunity to revise the assignment for resubmission.
Students who fail to complete this assignment or who do not earn a pass per the rubric after the allowed repeated
attempt will not meet the requirements for this course and will earn a grade of “F” for this course.
Theory and Lab Late Written Assignment Policy - Prelicensure Nursing
All assignments are expected to be submitted by the due date. It is the student's responsibility to verify the accuracy of
the submission, including the draft version and writing on assigned topics (if applicable). Late assignments will result in a
penalty of 25% per day beyond the due date.
Clinical Written Assignment Late Assignment Policy - Prelicensure Nursing
Clinical Written Assignments graded on a satisfactory/unsatisfactory and/or pass/fail rating scale are expected to be
submitted by the deadline. Only one clinical assignment per quarter per course may be submitted for a grade past the
due date with faculty and program administrator or designee approval due to an unavoidable emergency. Submission
of late assignments without faculty and program administrator or designee approval will result in an
unsatisfactory/failing rating. Unapproved late assignments may result in a course failure.
Unavoidable emergencies will be addressed on a case-by-case basis. Documentation must be submitted to the Makeup
Request Form within 48 hours of the due date. The targeted response time for approval/denial is 48 business hours.
Once an assignment has been graded, resubmissions for a higher grade are not allowed.
No assignments will be accepted after the official term end date.
Students are expected to take all exams and quizzes as scheduled. A student who will be late for or misses an exam or
quiz is expected to notify faculty in advance. Make-up quizzes and exams may be offered for those with unavoidable
emergencies. The make-up exam or quiz may be different in format from the originally administered version. The
decision to offer a make-up exam or quiz will be at the discretion of the Academic Leadership in collaboration with the
course faculty member. Documentation must be submitted within 48 business hours of the unavoidable emergency.
Documentation will be submitted via the Makeup Request Form. Make-up quizzes or exams are to be scheduled in
coordination with GEARS and Academic Leadership after the student returns to educational activities.
As part of Galen’s continued effort to offer courses of the highest quality and effectiveness, students will have the
opportunity to evaluate this course as well as provide feedback on course faculty. Evaluations will be distributed to
students prior to the end of the term. All evaluations are completely confidential and anonymous.

Your outcomes progress evaluation is an important part of the evaluation process. The specific purposes of
the outcomes progress evaluation are to (1) help you plan, organize, and document your learning during the
clinical practicum; (2) help faculty understand the degree of insight you have into your learning; and (3) help
you and the faculty to evaluate how you are meeting program outcomes.
1. A summary discussion of experiences and patients cared for. We consider families, parents, and
significant others important to discuss along with the primary patient.
2. Discuss utilization or incorporation of concepts from all previous courses - Include care related growth
and development, caring, advocacy, teaching, communication, culture and spirituality.
3. This one is very important: Note what you would do differently if you had the opportunity. We are
interested in decisions, actions, statements, and any other patient/community-oriented actions and
clinical decisions made. Include opportunities where you could have been more compassionate.
4. When the outcome progress evaluation is returned respond to comments (with contrasting color ink)
made on your work. This is critical, to ensure that you have an ongoing written dialogue.
Use the opportunity to reflect on both the transferable skills that you are developing, as well as the course-
specific skills you are putting into practice in the clinical area.

Clinical Evaluation Tool (CET) for all Clinical Nursing Courses & Evaluation Policies
Please note the clinical evaluation form for each clinical nursing course will be included in the
course syllabus when distributed to learners.
Galen College of Nursing Evaluation & Clinical Grading Policy
1. All course competencies must be met at the conclusion of the clinical nursing course at the
specified level in order to have a passing grade for the course.
All areas in the course must be at least a Satisfactory (S) in order to receive a passing grade.
FAILURE TO MEET COURSE COMPETENCIES AT THE SPECIFIED LEVEL WILL RESULT IN A CLINICAL
2. Any learner who shows evidence of unsafe behavior may be dismissed from the nursing program.
This will result in a grade of “F” for the course and excluded from attending the clinical practicum.
This may occur anytime during the course.
Examples of behaviors that would be deemed unsafe include:
• Operating beyond the identified role and scope of the learner at the course level.
• Behaviors that are unsafe and result in injury to a patient.
3. During each clinical nursing course, the learner will have a daily cumulative clinical evaluation based
on your daily clinical performance. In addition to the daily cumulative clinical evaluations, you will
have a mid-term and final clinical evaluation. The daily cumulative clinical evaluations and mid-term
are designed to be formative. The learner will self-evaluate using the course-specific evaluation tool
and will discuss the evaluation with the faculty during the mid-term and final CET. The cumulative
daily CET does not require the student to complete a self-evaluation. The learner and the faculty will
complete the mid-term self-evaluation form at the conclusion of the discussion. The final evaluation
will be summative and completed by the faculty at the conclusion of the course. The learner can
comment on the final evaluation form. Achieving a satisfactory rating on the final CET requires the
student to have a cumulative (≥74%) satisfactory or better rating on the cumulative daily CET.
